To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of PCM and EG as fillers in crude glycerol polyurethane foaming process can be used to improve the thermal properties and mechanical performance of the foams.
the incorporation of PCM and EG to crude glycerol PUFs increased their thermal conductivity and density, which limited the thermal energy storage.
the incorporation of PCM and EG to CG PUFs increased the stiffness of ensuing composites, but also increased the thermal conductivity and decreased the thermal storage capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new composite material with improved thermal properties, and the results obtained show that this new composite material could be used as a thermal insulator with a thermal energy storage capacity.

the design and development of a novel thermal storage material based on the combination of a bio-renewable resource (crude glycerol) with a bio-sourced PCM (palmitic acid) and a bio-renewably derived filler (expandable graphite).

the development of composite foams based on renewable resources (CG) with the aim of improving their thermal comfort properties by adding PCMs and EG, which is a novel approach to the use of PCMS in composite foams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of PCM and EG to PUFs increased the thermal and mechanical performance of PUFs, but also increased their density and conductivity.

the use of PCM and EG in CG derived PUFs can enhance the thermal performance of the ensuing composite foams but that their thermal conductivity and density must be taken into account when considering the use of these composite foams for thermal insulation applications.

, although the use of EG as a filler in the composite PUFs improved their thermal conductivity and mechanical properties, its incorporation did not significantly improve the thermal energy storage properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of EG in PUFs containing PCMs is a good solution to increase the thermal conductivity of PUF panels and to enhance the thermal buffering effect of the composite PUFs.
the use of EG as a filler in PUFs containing PCMs is a promising solution to improve the thermal properties of the ensuing composites.
the incorporation of EG in the composite PUFs is a promising solution to increase the thermal conductivity of these foams whilst keeping the thermal comfort and thermal buffering properties of PUFs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the addition of PCMs to PUFs can be a viable solution for thermal energy storage, however the incorporation of EG as a filler-reinforcing material should be avoided as it increases the thermal conductivity of the foams, which in turn, reduces their thermal energy storage capabilities.
the addition of PCM and EG can be used to improve the mechanical properties of the PUFs, but the thermal conductivity increase limits the thermal energy storage capacity of the PUF panel.

the use of EG in combination with PCM can be an effective strategy to enhance the mechanical performance of PUFs, and that numerical simulations can be a useful tool to predict the performance of composite PUFs with different compositions.
